ideas.hook: How to message a recruiter on LinkedIn (3 templates that don't sound like everyone else)
ideas.why: Competitor lesson from Weekday (free outreach writer targeting this exact search) and R&D Lab lead 'Write about the problem, not the extension': a problem-first page captures the search and sends readers to the extension.
ideas.script:
PAGE BRIEF: 'How to message a recruiter on LinkedIn' (free, problem-first)

Why: Weekday's free recruiter-message writer is aimed at exactly this search and funnels people into its own job products. R&D Lab lead 'Write about the problem, not the extension' says the same: answer the problem, then offer the tool. LinkedAI's edge is that it reads both profiles and finds the common ground itself.

Page title: How to message a recruiter on LinkedIn (3 templates that don't sound like everyone else)
Intro (2 sentences): Most cold messages say 'I'm interested in the role.' Here's what to write instead, and how to find something real you share with the person.

Section 1 - Find the common ground first: same school, same old employer, same project or group, same city, a post they wrote. Pick one specific thing.
Section 2 - Three templates (keep each short, one ask at the end):
 1. Shared school: 'Hi [name], I saw we both went to [school]. I'm applying for [role] at [company] and would value 10 minutes of your view on the team. Would that be okay?'
 2. Shared past employer: 'Hi [name], I noticed you worked at [company] before [current company]. I'm [one line about you] and interested in [role]. Could I ask one question about the team?'
 3. Their post: 'Hi [name], your post on [topic] made me think about [one specific thing]. I'm applying for [role]. Is [question] a fair thing to ask?'
Section 3 - Mistakes to skip: attaching your resume to the first message (a Weekday claim, not independently verified, so don't quote a number), asking for a job outright, writing a wall of text.
Section 4 - 'Skip the hunt for common ground': one short paragraph and a button to the LinkedAI Chrome Web Store page: 'LinkedAI reads your profile and theirs and writes the message around what you share. Free to start.'
SEO: target phrase 'how to message a recruiter on LinkedIn'; one H1; FAQ with 3 questions (Should I attach a resume? How long should it be? When should I follow up?). Don't invent statistics; cite a source for any number.
Where to put it: a page on the Agent HQ/LinkedAI site Omar controls, or a Chrome Web Store 'Website' link. Nothing here depends on a feature that isn't built yet.

[Talking to camera, phone in hand]
Only 2 to 3 percent of job applications turn into interviews. So I stopped applying. Well — I stopped ONLY applying.
Now for every job I actually want, I message someone on the team. The problem is cold messages sound cold. "Hi, I'm interested in the role" gets left on read.
[Screen recording: LinkedIn profile open, LinkedAI panel]
So I've been using this extension called LinkedAI. You open someone's profile and it finds real common ground between you two — same school, same old company, a project you both worked on — and writes the message around that.
[Point at screen]
Look — it caught that we both interned at the same place. I would never have noticed that.
That's the difference between being ignored and getting "sure, happy to chat."
[Back to camera]
It's free on the Chrome Web Store. Link's in my bio. Go message someone today.

ideas.title: Your cover letter sounds like a robot
ideas.hook: If your cover letter starts with 'I am excited to apply,' the recruiter already knows.
ideas.why: Reviewers of Simplify+ and Jobscan keep calling their AI writing generic or keyword-stuffed, and those tools charge $40–50 a month. Tailored-from-the-actual-job-post is the gap.
ideas.script:
[Talking to camera, a bit dramatic]
If your cover letter starts with "I am excited to apply," the recruiter already knows. A chatbot wrote it — and so did the other 200 people.
The fix isn't writing it yourself at 2am. It's giving the AI the actual job post.
[Screen recording: LinkedIn job page]
I use this Chrome extension called LinkedAI. You open the job on LinkedIn, it pulls the whole posting — requirements, tools, the weird specific stuff — and builds a resume and cover letter that match THAT job. Not a template.
[Scroll the generated letter]
See how it mentions the exact tools they listed? That's what gets you past the filter and makes a human actually read it.
You can get both together as a bundle, which is cheaper than doing them one by one.
[Back to camera]
It's on the Chrome Web Store, free to try. Link in bio. Stop sending robot letters.

ideas.title: UGC brief: 'The recruiter has AI. So should you.'
ideas.hook: Recruiters are using AI to filter you out. Here's the AI I use back.
ideas.why: Sponsored creator reads like @charlottechaze's Tsenta video use the 'their AI vs. your AI' angle with a trial link. Jobright is only starting on referral outreach, so LinkedAI can own 'AI that gets you a real conversation'.
ideas.script:
WHO: Job-seeking creators (students, new grads, career switchers), 5k–100k followers, face-to-camera style.
PAY: Flat fee + affiliate commission on Pro signups via their link.
LENGTH: 30–45s, vertical, natural lighting, phone screen recording for the demo.
ANGLE: "Recruiters use AI to filter you. I use AI to skip the pile." You're a job seeker who found a useful tool — never imply you know the founder or helped build it.
STRUCTURE:
1) Hook (first 2s): the recruiter-AI line, or your own version of it.
2) The pain: applying to dozens of jobs and hearing nothing.
3) Demo 1: open a LinkedIn job → LinkedAI makes a resume + cover letter matched to that post.
4) Demo 2: open a hiring manager's profile → LinkedAI finds something you have in common and writes the message. Show the common-ground line on screen.
5) Result: what you'd send / what happened (only real results).
6) CTA: "It's free on the Chrome Web Store — my link's in bio."
MUST: Disclose as an ad (#ad or paid partnership label). Don't promise interviews or jobs. Don't name competitors or quote their prices.
AVOID: Reading a script word for word; overselling.

ideas.formatted:
**VERSION B - Vulnerable admission (~45s)**
- **Why this one:** Directly counters the 'volume' strategy of competitors like AIApply.
- **On-screen text (first 3-5s):** I was applying to 100 jobs a week

**Scene 1 - Hook (0-3s)**
> I was applying to 100 jobs a week and getting zero responses.

*Delivery:* flat and serious.

[pause]

**Scene 2 - Context lean (~8s)**
> I thought volume was the answer. I used every auto-apply tool I could find.

*Delivery:* casual.

[pause]

**Scene 3 - Re-hook (~20s)**
> But here's the part nobody mentions: recruiters can spot a 'bulk' application from a mile away.

*Delivery:* lean in.

[pause]

**Scene 4 - Value (~30s)**
> I switched to LinkedAI. It doesn't spam. It just helps me customize my outreach so I'm actually talking to a human.

*Delivery:* casual.

[pause]

**Scene 5 - Payoff (~40s)**
> It's on the Chrome store. Search Growth Architect.

*Delivery:* casual.

[pause]

**Last line:** "Quality wins every time."

  - Bulk applying is a waste of time. (Call-out)
  - Stop spamming recruiters. (Hard truth)

ideas.title: SEO Page: Common Ground Outreach
ideas.why: Lesson from Weekday: use a free, search-optimized tool to capture traffic for 'how to message a recruiter', then funnel to the LinkedAI extension.
ideas.details: Create a page 'How to Message a Recruiter on LinkedIn' with a free text-input tool that generates a personalized message based on common ground. When they click 'copy', offer the Chrome extension for one-click automation.

items.title: Pricing opacity as a growth lever
items.creator: Simplify / Teal
items.metric: Most competitors hide monthly/annual pricing behind weekly tiers.
items.whyItWorks: LinkedAI can win by being the only transparent option in the market.

items.title: Single-utility SEO pages
items.creator: Weekday
items.metric: High organic traffic from 'how to message recruiter' keywords.
items.whyItWorks: Proves that a simple, free tool drives more users than complex dashboards.

items.title: Teal's weekly pricing increased, AI content can be generic or fabricate details
items.creator: Teal (via reviewers)
items.whyItWorks: Competitor's confusing/expensive billing and AI quality issues are a strong differentiator for LinkedAI's transparent pricing and authentic AI.

items.title: Simplify lacks public pricing and free trial, AI output needs substantial editing
items.creator: Simplify (via reviewers)
items.whyItWorks: LinkedAI can gain trust by being transparent about pricing and emphasizing quality AI output that requires less editing.

items.title: Careerflow's free tier is limited, AI mock interviews are 'thin', and renewals can be surprising
items.creator: Careerflow (via reviewers)
items.whyItWorks: LinkedAI can offer a more generous free plan and clear communication about renewals. Also, focus on core strengths over 'thin' features.

items.title: Kickresume's per-job tailoring is weak, and AI usage has limits
items.creator: Kickresume (via reviewers)
items.whyItWorks: LinkedAI can highlight its strength in specific job tailoring and offer more flexible AI usage compared to competitors.

items.title: Jobscan's AI rewrite feature produces generic language and isn't checked against user's resume
items.creator: Jobscan (via reviewers)
items.whyItWorks: LinkedAI can differentiate by ensuring its AI output is authentic, non-generic, and accurately reflects the user's resume.

items.title: AIApply's auto-apply sends poor-fit jobs, has confusing add-on pricing, and an F-rating with BBB
items.creator: AIApply (via reviewers, BBB)
items.whyItWorks: LinkedAI can position itself as a tool for 'fewer, better messages' with accurate targeting and transparent pricing, countering AIApply's issues.

items.title: Taplio's Starter plan does not include AI features, high entry price for AI, and automation risks TOS violations
items.creator: Taplio (via reviewers)
items.metric: AI features start at Growth plan ($69/month); auto-DMs/connections risk LinkedIn TOS
items.whyItWorks: LinkedAI can offer clear AI feature availability at lower tiers and emphasize ethical, TOS-compliant automation for job search.

items.title: Gen Z increasingly uses TikTok for job search, surpassing LinkedIn for some
items.creator: VICE
items.metric: 22.1% of Gen Z use TikTok vs 20.8% LinkedIn for job search
items.whyItWorks: TikTok is a crucial platform for reaching job seekers; short-form video promos are highly relevant.

items.title: Videos explaining LinkedIn's new AI-powered job search and profile optimization are performing well
items.creator: YouTube creators
items.whyItWorks: Directly addresses user need for understanding and leveraging AI in job search, a perfect fit for LinkedAI's features.

items.title: Short videos demonstrating AI agents that rewrite LinkedIn profiles based on resume and job description are popular
items.creator: YouTube creators
items.whyItWorks: Highlights a direct use case for LinkedAI's profile optimization features, especially when emphasizing accuracy and authenticity.

items.title: Weekday offers a free recruiter outreach writer, targeting 'how to message a recruiter on LinkedIn'
items.creator: Weekday
items.whyItWorks: This is a direct competitor for LinkedAI's outreach feature. LinkedAI can differentiate by automatically finding common ground.

items.title: Simplify's founder post pitched one clear promise and got a 2,000-person waitlist
items.creator: Michael Yan / Simplify
items.whyItWorks: A single plain promise to a pain people already feel beat cold emails. LinkedAI's promise is a message that finds real common ground; lead every video with that one outcome.

items.title: 60-second green-screen job video topped 182,000 views
items.creator: Makena Yee (via The Interview Guys)
items.whyItWorks: Job-hunt videos with a face, a clear first-3-seconds claim and visual proof travel. Creators for LinkedAI should show the extension on a real profile in the first 5 seconds.

items.title: Job seekers say TikTok now beats LinkedIn for finding work; 2-3% of applications reach interviews
items.creator: VICE (Josh Katz video resume: 'hundreds of thousands of views')
items.metric: 22.1% of Gen Z use TikTok vs 20.8% LinkedIn for job search (per article)
items.whyItWorks: The audience already hangs out on TikTok and distrusts the apply button. A 'stop only applying' angle is credible there.

items.title: Free 'recruiter outreach writer' page targets 'how to message a recruiter on LinkedIn'
items.creator: Weekday
items.whyItWorks: A rival is using a free SEO tool to collect people who want to message recruiters. LinkedAI can answer the same search with a page and win on finding common ground automatically.

items.title: Teal+ sells a $13/week option reviewers call a dark pattern
items.creator: Teal (via MakerStack)
items.whyItWorks: Billing distrust is a gap. A clear monthly and yearly (20% off) Pro with no weekly trap is an easy comparison point in videos.

items.title: Simplify+ sells AI answers at $19.99/week or $39.99/month — reviewers call them generic
items.creator: Simplify (via ResumeHog review)
items.whyItWorks: The biggest free autofill tool charges ~$40/mo for AI writing people say sounds robotic. LinkedAI can win on 'sounds like you, not a bot' and a cheaper Pro.

items.title: Jobright raised its Turbo plan from $29.99 to $39.99/month; 'Insider Connections' referral feature is thin
items.creator: Jobright (via ResumeHog review)
items.whyItWorks: A big rival is moving toward referral outreach but only surfaces names. LinkedAI's common-ground messages are the step they're missing — and LinkedAI isn't US-only.

items.title: Jobscan charges $49.95/month; free plan is 5 scans and rewrites can turn keyword-stuffed
items.creator: Jobscan (via The Interview Guys)
items.whyItWorks: Job seekers between jobs feel these prices. A resume + cover letter bundle priced well under $50 is an easy comparison to make in videos and on the store listing.

items.title: LinkedIn's Hiring Assistant now plugs into ATSs like Greenhouse and Workday; LinkedIn claims 66% higher InMail acceptance
items.creator: LinkedIn (via Business Today, Sep 3 2026)
items.metric: Claimed 80% fewer profiles reviewed, +66% InMail acceptance
items.whyItWorks: Recruiters are leaning on AI to filter applicants, so cold applications matter less and direct, personal messages matter more — exactly LinkedAI's outreach pitch.

items.title: Paid creator read: 'Recruiters use AI to filter you out, so use your own AI' (Tsenta partner video)
items.creator: @charlottechaze on TikTok
items.whyItWorks: This is the exact sponsored-creator format Omar wants: an 'us vs. the recruiter's AI' hook, a free-trial link, and an 'I only partner with brands I believe in' line. A good template for LinkedAI UGC briefs.

brief.headline: Counter bulk-automation noise with 'Quality Outreach' and transparent pricing
brief.summary: Competitors like AIApply and Teal are struggling with trust and generic, high-volume automation. LinkedAI should lean into 'fewer, better' messages and transparent pricing to win trust.
